candidates: Do not use `optionalEnvToBoolean()` to gate logic on environment variables that hold non-boolean values such as semicolon-delimited path lists (e.g., `STORYBOOK_COMPONENT_PATHS`); use a dedicated parsing helper such as `getComponentTestPaths().length > 0` to check whether the variable contains meaningful data.

Model result objects that have a `success` boolean discriminant as a discriminated union (`{ success: true; field: string } | { success: false; error: string }`) rather than a flat interface with all properties optional; TypeScript will then narrow the type automatically inside `if (result.success)` branches, eliminating unsafe non-null assertions on success-only fields.

All `vi.mock()` calls must include `{ spy: true }` as the options argument per the project's Vitest mocking guidelines; this applies to both factory-style and simple mocks, including mocks for `node:fs`, `node:fs/promises`, and internal Storybook packages.

When spying on `console` methods with `vi.spyOn(console, ...)` in a test file, call `.mockRestore()` in an `afterAll` hook to restore the original implementations and prevent suppressed output from leaking into other test files.

Use optional chaining (`?.`) consistently throughout a property access chain on a potentially-null value; avoid mixing `value?.prop` with `value['key']` (a non-optional bracket access) on the same nullable object — use `value?.['key']` for bracket access.

Never merge code that contains a commented-out early `return` paired with an explicit 'TODO: uncomment this' or 'DO NOT MERGE WITH THIS' marker; restore the guard logic before the PR is merged so the intended skip/bail-out behavior actually executes.

When checking whether an ArgType entry is required in `generateDummyArgsFromArgTypes`, read `argType.required` directly (as defined on `InputType`), not `argType.type.required`; `SBType` does not have a `required` field, so the nested check always evaluates to `false` and all props are silently treated as optional.

Integration test snapshot values for generated dummy arguments must match what `generateDummyValueFromSBType` actually returns; cross-check against the unit assertions in `get-dummy-args-from-argtypes.test.ts` to catch mismatches (e.g., `{ name: 'number' }` returns `0`, not an arbitrary integer).

Never call `.sort()` directly on a module-level constant array (e.g., `CATEGORIZATION_RULES.sort(...)`); this mutates the shared reference on every invocation. Pre-compute a sorted copy at module initialization (`const SORTED_RULES = [...CATEGORIZATION_RULES].sort(...)`) and reference that constant instead.

Keep inline test comments synchronized with the implementation values they describe; if a threshold or constant changes in the source (e.g., the complexity cutoff in `get-candidates.ts`), update the corresponding test comment to reflect the exact current value.

Guard `sampleCount`/`sampleSize` parameters in `getCandidatesForStorybook` and `getComponentCandidates` against zero, negative, and non-finite inputs at the top of the function; `Array.slice(0, sampleCount)` with `sampleCount <= 0` returns an empty or reversed result rather than a meaningful sample — return safe defaults early instead.

Debug log messages should reference the variable they actually describe (use `candidates.length` after filtering, not `files.length` from the glob results); error return payloads should include the actual captured error message rather than a generic fixed string like `'Failed to find candidates'`.

When checking whether a rendered canvas element has content in `test-annotations.ts`, use `canvasElement.firstElementChild` (which returns only `Element` nodes) rather than `canvasElement.firstChild`; `firstChild` can return a `Text` or `Comment` node, and calling `getBoundingClientRect()` or `getComputedStyle()` on it will throw.

In the component transformer's `ExportNamedDeclaration` specifier path, call `addComponent(exported.name, ...)` for function and class declarations rather than `addComponent(bindingNodeId.name, ...)`; for `export { Foo as Bar }`, the component must be registered under its exported alias `Bar`, not the local name `Foo`.

When generating AST object property keys with Babel in the component transformer, use `t.isValidIdentifier(key) ? t.identifier(key) : t.stringLiteral(key)` for every key; unconditionally using `t.identifier(key)` emits invalid JavaScript for keys such as `data-testid`, `aria-label`, or names that start with a digit.

Tests asserting regex-escaping behavior must use input patterns that actually contain regex-special characters (e.g., parentheses, square brackets, dots); using only alphanumeric and hyphen characters exercises no escaping code path, so a broken escaper would still pass the test.

When building `PackageGroupResult` maps using `getSafeVersionSpecifier()` (which returns `string | null`), align the container type to allow `null` values (`Record<string, string | null>`) or normalize `null → undefined` at every assignment site; the mismatch with the declared `string | undefined` type surfaces as a TypeScript error under strict mode.

Do not annotate `cached()` wrappers with `: any`; let TypeScript infer the wrapped function's type (as done for `cachedReadFileSync` and `cachedFindUp` in `code/renderers/react/src/componentManifest/utils.ts`), or supply the exact function signature if inference fails.

When mocking a function in a test, use a return value that matches the actual return type of the real function; avoid `undefined as unknown as ReturnType<typeof fn>` casts that hide a type mismatch — e.g., mock `findConfigFile` (which returns `string | null`) with `null`, not `undefined`.

The regex used to extract npm dependency names from Vitest/Vite stack traces must support scoped packages; replace the pattern `[^/.]+` with `(?:@[^/]+\/)?[^/.]+` so `@tanstack/query` is captured in full rather than just `@tanstack`.

After calling `getComponentComplexity()`, validate the result with `Number.isFinite(complexity)` before using it in sorting or averaging; edge-case parsing errors or division by zero can produce `NaN`/`Infinity`, which corrupts candidate selection and average metrics.

Use template literals for debug log messages that include computed values (e.g., `` `Selected ${candidates.length} files` `` rather than `'candidates files:' + candidates.length`), and log error objects directly (or via `.message`) rather than via template interpolation, which produces `[object Object]`.

When checking CSS `opacity` for visibility in `isEmptyRender`, compare numerically (`parseFloat(style.opacity) > 0`) rather than via string equality (`style.opacity !== '0'`); browsers may return `'0.0'` or `'0.00'`, which string comparison incorrectly treats as visible.

Never use an empty `catch {}` block in Storybook `afterEach` hooks (e.g., in `test-annotations.ts`); caught errors must be forwarded to `reporting.addReport()` following the pattern established in the a11y addon's `afterEach` (`code/addons/a11y/src/preview.tsx`) so failures are visible in test results.

Verify that import paths in test files resolve to the module that actually exports the imported symbol; an incorrect sibling path (e.g., importing `extractCategorizedErrors` from `./categorize-render-errors` when it lives in `./parse-vitest-report`) produces a silent `undefined` import rather than a clear compile error.

In `get-known-packages.ts`, wrap each `getActualPackageVersion()` call in a per-item try-catch (or use `Promise.allSettled`) so that one failing package resolution does not reject the entire `Promise.all` and crash the telemetry analysis; fall back to the raw version string from `allDependencies[dep]` on error.

In `parseVitestResults`, replace the `any` parameter with minimal structural types (`VitestRunResult`, `VitestSuiteResult`, `VitestAssertionResult`) and guard against missing arrays with `Array.isArray() / ?? []`; derive fallback counts from parsed results when `numTotalTests`/`numPassedTests`/`numFailedTests` are undefined, and clamp `passed - passedButEmptyRender` to `>= 0` with `Math.max(0, ...)` to prevent negative success rates.

Every value of `ERROR_CATEGORIES` must have an explicit `case` in `getCategoryDescription` returning a specific, actionable description; do not allow any defined category (including `SERVER_COMPONENTS_ERROR` and `UNKNOWN_ERROR`) to fall through to the generic default message.

Per the project's Vitest mocking guidelines, configure or override mock implementations in `beforeEach` blocks (or a nested `describe`'s `beforeEach`), not inline within individual test bodies; test cases should contain only assertions and the invocation of the subject under test.

In `extractCategorizedErrors`, type the `reduce` accumulator precisely (e.g., `Record<ErrorCategory, CategorizedError>`) rather than `Record<string, any>`; the precise type is expressible and prevents silent type errors at call sites.

Negative-only assertions (e.g., `expect(result.code).not.toContain(...)`) in component-transformer tests should be paired with a positive assertion confirming the transform actually ran (e.g., that `getComponentArgTypes` was called, or that the output contains a generated `describe`/`it` block); without it, a regression that silently produces no output still passes the negative assertion.

When a string variable defaults to `''` (empty string, not `null`/`undefined`) and an empty value should trigger a fallback, use `||` rather than `??`; nullish coalescing only triggers on `null`/`undefined` and returns `''` unchanged.

Captured error variables in `catch` blocks (e.g., `const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)`) must be used — either logged or included in the returned error payload; leaving the variable unused silently discards diagnostic information.

When calling `executeCommand` (or any child-process spawner) with a custom `env` object, always spread `process.env` first (`{ ...process.env, CUSTOM_VAR: value }`) to inherit `PATH`, `NODE_ENV`, and other required variables; providing only custom keys without the parent environment will break the spawned process.

Type-guard functions that use the `in` operator to check for a property (e.g., `'elements' in value`) must first verify the value is a non-null object (`value !== null && typeof value === 'object'`); applying `in` to `null` or a primitive throws a TypeError.

In `getComponentDocgen`, prefer `docgens.find(d => d.exportName === 'default') ?? docgens[0]` over plain `docgens[0]` when no `componentName` is provided; react-docgen may return components in any order, so relying on array position to identify the default export is non-deterministic.

Test assertions for timing-based telemetry stats (`candidateAnalysisDuration`, `totalRunDuration`, `testRunDuration`) should use `expect.any(Number)` rather than exact values; even near-instant async operations can produce non-zero durations under load, making exact-value assertions flaky.
